questions.stem: What is the word equation for aerobic respiration?

options.text: Glucose + oxygen -> carbon dioxide + water + energy

questions.explanation: Aerobic respiration uses glucose and oxygen to produce carbon dioxide, water, and energy (released as ATP). It occurs in the mitochondria.

questions.stem: Where in the cell does aerobic respiration mainly take place?
questions.explanation: Aerobic respiration mainly takes place in the mitochondria. Some initial stages (glycolysis) occur in the cytoplasm, but most ATP is produced in the mitochondria.

questions.stem: Why is aerobic respiration described as an exothermic reaction?

options.text: It releases energy that can be used by the cell
It absorbs energy from the surroundings

questions.explanation: Aerobic respiration is exothermic because it releases energy. The chemical energy stored in glucose is transferred to ATP and some is released as heat.

questions.stem: What is the energy released during respiration used for?

options.text: Muscle contraction, active transport, protein synthesis, nerve impulses, and maintaining body temperature

questions.explanation: Energy from respiration is used for many vital processes including muscle contraction, active transport of substances, building proteins from amino acids, transmitting nerve impulses, and maintaining body temperature.

questions.stem: Is respiration the same as breathing?

options.text: Yes, they are the same thing
No, breathing is the mechanical process of moving air; respiration is the chemical reaction in cells

questions.explanation: Breathing (ventilation) is the physical process of moving air in and out of the lungs. Respiration is the chemical process that occurs in every living cell, releasing energy from glucose.

options.text: Yes, all living cells respire continuously, including plant cells

questions.explanation: All living cells respire continuously, including plant cells. Plants respire 24 hours a day. During the day, photosynthesis also occurs, but this is a separate process.

questions.stem: How much ATP does aerobic respiration produce per molecule of glucose compared to anaerobic?

options.text: Aerobic respiration does not produce ATP
Much more - approximately 38 ATP compared to 2 ATP

questions.explanation: Aerobic respiration is much more efficient, producing approximately 38 molecules of ATP per glucose molecule, compared to only 2 ATP from anaerobic respiration. This is because glucose is completely broken down.
